text: This BrainFrame demo is shared by E topus, a chipset company in Silicon Valley.
You can see that the YOLO V 10 model is loaded into BrainFrame.

The YOLO model is trained to detect the chipset position in the socket during the chipset testing process. The pure green bounding box shows that a wrong chipset position is detected when the chip is not in the socket.
At the bottom right of the screen, the robot control software receives the detection results and prints 'wrong'.
So the system moves the robot arm to reposition the chip.
The detection bounding box turns yellow-green, indicating that the robot arm has moved the chip to the correct position.
At the bottom right of the screen, the robot control software receives the detection results and prints 'correct'.

Whether you need to build AI vision for a robot arm on a factory production line or for humanoid robots, connect thousands of cameras in a data center for enterprise business analytics, or set up an AI security patrol for your own home, BrainFrame handles it all smoothly, on-premises or in the cloud.
